title: Short Introduction to BAMP
text: Age-period-cohort (APC) models decompose incidence mortality rates three smooth components: age effect (risk varies across age groups), period effect (risk varies calendar time) cohort effect (risk varies across birth cohorts). BAMP fits models Bayesian framework via MCMC provides tools check convergence, inspect fitted effects, predict future cases.

title: Short Introduction to BAMP
text: BAMP includes data example: cases population, matrices observed case counts population risk, cross-classified calendar year (rows) age group (columns).  simulating APC data, see vignette(“simulation”, package=“bamp”).
code: data(apc) plot(cases[,1],type="l",ylim=range(cases), ylab="cases", xlab="year", main="cases per age group") for (i in 2:8)lines(cases[,i], col=i)

what: APC model with random-walk first-order priors
title: Short Introduction to BAMP
text: fit model first-order random walk ("rw1") prior age, period cohort effects – common default assumes effect changes smoothly, without systematic trend, neighbouring levels. periods_per_agegroup tells bamp() many calendar years age group spans, needed map age period onto cohort dimension. bamp() automatically checks MCMC convergence using Gelman-Rubin diagnostic warns chains converged. can also run check manually: print() summarises fitted model: posterior estimates smoothing (precision) parameters, deviance DIC, useful comparing models (see vignette(“modeling”, package=“bamp”) model selection): fitted age, period cohort effects can plotted point-wise posterior quantiles:  default plot shows median 90% interval; quantiles can requested explicitly:  prior choices (e.g. second-order random walks, heterogeneity, covariates), see vignette(“modeling”, package=“bamp”).
code: model1 <- bamp(cases, population, age="rw1", period="rw1", cohort="rw1",               periods_per_agegroup = 5) checkConvergence(model1) ## [1] TRUE print(model1) ##  ##  Model: ## age (rw1)  - period (rw1)  - cohort (rw1) model ## Deviance:     230.12 ## pD:            36.60 ## DIC:          266.72 ##  ##  ##  Hyper parameters:                 5%           50%          95%          ## age                              0.436        1.108        2.295 ## period                          48.842      128.964      320.787 ## cohort                          35.190       61.080      103.190 ##  ##  ## Markov Chains convergence checked succesfully using Gelman's R (potential scale reduction factor). plot(model1) plot(model1, quantiles = c(0.025,0.1,0.5,0.9,0.975))

title: Short Introduction to BAMP
text: period cohort effects modelled random walks, likely continuation flat extrapolation growing uncertainty – lets us predict cases upcoming years: plot shows predicted probability case per age group; dashed vertical line marks start 3-year forecast:  details, see vignette(“prediction”, package=“bamp”).
code: pred <- predict_apc(object=model1, periods=3) m<-max(pred$pr[2,,]) plot(pred$pr[2,,8],type="l", ylab="probability", xlab="year", ylim=c(0,m)) for (i in 7:1)   lines(pred$pr[2,,i],col=8-i) legend(1,m,col=8:1,legend=paste("Age group",1:8),lwd=2,cex=0.6) lines(c(10.5,10.5),c(0,1),lty=2)

what: APC model with random-walk first-order priors
title: Bayesian Age-Period-Cohort Modeling
text: first-order random walk ("rw1") prior assumes effect changes smoothly, without systematic trend, neighbouring age groups, periods cohorts. common default. bamp() automatically checks MCMC convergence using Gelman-Rubin diagnostic. can also run check manually: print() summarises fitted model: posterior estimates smoothing (precision) parameters, deviance DIC, useful comparing models fitted vignette: fitted age, period cohort effects can plotted point-wise posterior quantiles:  default plot shows median 90% interval; quantiles can requested explicitly:
code: model1 <- bamp(cases, population, age="rw1", period="rw1", cohort="rw1",               periods_per_agegroup = 5) checkConvergence(model1) ## [1] TRUE print(model1) ##  ##  Model: ## age (rw1)  - period (rw1)  - cohort (rw1) model ## Deviance:     230.12 ## pD:            36.60 ## DIC:          266.72 ##  ##  ##  Hyper parameters:                 5%           50%          95%          ## age                              0.436        1.108        2.295 ## period                          48.842      128.964      320.787 ## cohort                          35.190       61.080      103.190 ##  ##  ## Markov Chains convergence checked succesfully using Gelman's R (potential scale reduction factor). plot(model1) plot(model1, quantiles = c(0.025,0.1,0.5,0.9,0.975))

what: APC model with random-walk second-order priors
title: Bayesian Age-Period-Cohort Modeling
text: second-order random walk ("rw2") prior penalises curvature rather level, produces effects follow smooth, roughly linear trend instead reverting towards constant. RW2 priors less informative RW1, chains mix slowly need substantially iterations converge; also set smoothing hyperparameters explicitly instead using defaults.
code: model2 <- bamp(cases, population, age="rw2", period="rw2", cohort="rw2",               periods_per_agegroup = 5,               mcmc.options=list("number_of_iterations"=200000, "burn_in"=100000, "step"=50, "tuning"=500),               hyperpar=list("age"=c(1,.5), "period"=c(1,0.05), "cohort"=c(1,0.05))) checkConvergence(model2) ## [1] TRUE print(model2) ##  ##  Model: ## age (rw2)  - period (rw2)  - cohort (rw2) model ## Deviance:     233.58 ## pD:            35.72 ## DIC:          269.30 ##  ##  ##  Hyper parameters:                 5%           50%          95%          ## age                              1.090        3.024        6.847 ## period                          16.052       41.275       91.027 ## cohort                          24.825       46.878       83.398 ##  ##  ## Markov Chains convergence checked succesfully using Gelman's R (potential scale reduction factor). plot(model2)

what: APC model without a period effect
title: Bayesian Age-Period-Cohort Modeling
text: Age, period cohort linearly dependent – one determined two – model three unrestricted smooth trends identifiable. One common way sidestep drop effect least interest – period effect (period=" ") – keep age cohort:
code: model3<-bamp(cases, population, age="rw1", period=" ", cohort="rw2",               periods_per_agegroup = 5) checkConvergence(model3) ## [1] TRUE print(model3) ##  ##  Model: ## age (rw1) cohort (rw2) model ## Deviance:     275.82 ## pD:            29.69 ## DIC:          305.52 ##  ##  ##  Hyper parameters:                 5%           50%          95%          ## age                              0.299        0.724        1.497 ## cohort                          36.892       73.124      139.543 ##  ##  ## Markov Chains convergence checked succesfully using Gelman's R (potential scale reduction factor). plot(model3)

what: APC model with a cohort covariate
title: Bayesian Age-Period-Cohort Modeling
text: Instead dropping effect, known covariate can scale : cohort_covariate multiplies cohort effect given value cohort (bundled example covariate cov_c), useful external, cohort-specific risk factor available.
code: (model4<-bamp(cases, population, age="rw1", period="rw1", cohort="rw1",              cohort_covariate = cov_c, periods_per_agegroup = 5)) ##  ##  Model: ## age (rw1)  - period (rw1)  - cohort (rw1) model ## Deviance:     230.43 ## pD:            37.39 ## DIC:          267.81 ##  ##  ##  Hyper parameters:                 5%           50%          95%          ## age                              0.408        1.021        2.101 ## period                          55.546      142.037      349.491 ## cohort                          31.623       54.483       92.487 ##  ##  ## Markov Chains convergence checked succesfully using Gelman's R (potential scale reduction factor). plot(model4)

what: APC model with a period covariate
title: Bayesian Age-Period-Cohort Modeling
text: Analogously, period_covariate scales period effect known, period-specific covariate (cov_p):
code: (model5<-bamp(cases, population, age="rw1", period="rw1", cohort="rw1",              period_covariate = cov_p, periods_per_agegroup = 5)) ##  ##  Model: ## age (rw1)  - period (rw1)  - cohort (rw1) model ## Deviance:     229.64 ## pD:            36.71 ## DIC:          266.35 ##  ##  ##  Hyper parameters:                 5%           50%          95%          ## age                              0.442        1.098        2.226 ## period                          54.273      147.975      384.812 ## cohort                          34.560       60.147       98.309 ##  ##  ## Markov Chains convergence checked succesfully using Gelman's R (potential scale reduction factor). plot(model5)

title: Bayesian Age-Period-Cohort Prediction
text: period cohort effects modelled random walks, can extrapolated continuation trends, lets predict_apc() forecast cases years beyond observed data. first introduction bamp(), see vignette(“bamp”, package=“bamp”); model specifications, see vignette(“modeling”, package=“bamp”). use bundled data example, covers ten years:  see well forecast holds real data, fit model first nine years predict tenth, can compared cases actually observed year. predict_apc() extends fitted model given number periods. update = TRUE forecast merged back model0 (model0$predicted) instead returned separate object: forecast year 10 (dashed lines: 90% credible interval; solid line: median) lines well true total cases (points), held fit:  credible intervals extend period cohort effects year 10:
code: data(apc) plot(cases[,1],type="l",ylim=range(cases), ylab="cases", xlab="year", main="cases per age group") for (i in 2:8)lines(cases[,i], col=i) model0 <- bamp(cases[-10,], population[-10,], age="rw1", period="rw1", cohort="rw1",               periods_per_agegroup = 5) model0<-predict_apc(object=model0, periods=1, population=population, update = TRUE) ts.plot(t(model0$predicted$cases_period), lty=c(2,1,2)) points(apply(cases,1,sum), pch=19) ts.plot(t(model0$predicted$period), lty=c(2,1,2)) ts.plot(t(model0$predicted$cohort), lty=c(2,1,2))

title: Simulating Age-Period-Cohort Data
text: first fix three true effects log-odds scale; centred (mean zero) since shape, level, identified (see vignette(“modeling”, package=“bamp”)). age effect increasing, concave curve:  period effect V-shaped: falls first half observed periods, rises second half:  cohort effect falls earliest cohorts, rises middle ones, slightly falls recent cohorts. periods_per_agegroup = 5 10 age groups spanning 25 periods, periods_per_agegroup * (10 - 1) + 25 = 70 cohorts:
code: age=2*sqrt(seq(1,20,length=10)) age<- age-mean(age) plot(age, type="l") period=25:1 period[13:25]<-13:25 period<-period/5 period<-period-mean(period) plot(period, type="l") periods_per_agegroup=5 number_of_cohorts <- periods_per_agegroup*(10-1)+25 cohort<-rep(0,70) cohort[1:20]<-(19:0) cohort[21:40]<- (1:20)/2 cohort[41:70]<- 10 cohort=cohort-(1:70)/10 cohort<-cohort/10 cohort<-cohort-mean(cohort) plot(cohort, type="l")

title: Simulating Age-Period-Cohort Data
text: fit first-order random-walk model used throughout vignettes simulated data:  Since know true effects (unlike real data), can check directly well bamp() recovered : black line true effect, blue line fitted posterior median (effects()). age, period cohort effects identified shared linear trend (see vignette(“modeling”, package=“bamp”)), recovered curves show nonlinear (curvature) features truth, linearly shifted relative .
code: simmod <- bamp(cases = simdata$cases, population = simdata$population, age = "rw2", period = "rw2", cohort = "rw2", periods_per_agegroup =periods_per_agegroup) print(simmod) ##  ##  Model: ## age (rw2)  - period (rw2)  - cohort (rw2) model ## Deviance:     252.83 ## pD:            40.63 ## DIC:          293.46 ##  ##  ##  Hyper parameters:                 5%           50%          95%          ## age                              3.148        7.788       16.062 ## period                         146.307      282.779      504.666 ## cohort                         991.512     1827.299     3301.015 ##  ##  ## Markov Chains convergence checked succesfully using Gelman's R (potential scale reduction factor). par(mfrow=c(3,1)) plot(simmod) effects<-effects(simmod) plot(age, type="l") lines(effects$age, col="blue") plot(period, type="l", ylim=range(effects$period)) lines(effects$period, col="blue") plot(cohort, type="l", ylim=range(effects$cohort)) lines(effects$cohort, col="blue")

title: Simulating Age-Period-Cohort Data
text: vignette(“prediction”, package=“bamp”), fitted random walks can extrapolated forecast cases periods beyond simulated data – 5 , supplied population array covers 30 periods (25 observed + 5 forecast) across 10 age groups: Total predicted cases per period shown median (solid points) 80% credible interval (dashes):  period effect extends way 5 forecast periods:
code: prediction<-predict_apc(simmod, periods=5, population=array(1e6,c(30,10)), quantiles=c(.1,.5,.9)) plot(prediction$cases_period[2,], ylim=range(prediction$cases_period),ylab="",pch=19) points(prediction$cases_period[1,],pch="–",cex=2) points(prediction$cases_period[3,],pch="–",cex=2) for (i in 1:30)lines(rep(i,3),prediction$cases_period[,i]) plot(prediction$period[2,], type="l", ylim=range(prediction$period)) points(prediction$period[2,1:25]) for (i in 26:30)lines(rep(i,3),prediction$period[,i])

title: Simulating Age-Period-Cohort Data
text: Finally, refit simulated data period covariate scaling period effect (see vignette(“modeling”, package=“bamp”)). period covariate positive multiplier, must larger zero.
code: cov_p<-exp(rnorm(30,period,.1)) simmod2 <- bamp(cases = simdata$cases, population = simdata$population, age = "rw1", period = "rw1", cohort = "rw1", periods_per_agegroup = periods_per_agegroup, period_covariate = cov_p) print(simmod2) ##  ##  Model: ## age (rw1)  - period (rw1)  - cohort (rw1) model ## Deviance:     253.92 ## pD:            69.51 ## DIC:          323.43 ##  ##  ##  Hyper parameters:                 5%           50%          95%          ## age                              0.677        1.527        2.951 ## period                           1.947        3.450        5.928 ## cohort                          77.981      116.366      167.747 ##  ##  ## Markov Chains convergence checked succesfully using Gelman's R (potential scale reduction factor). par(mfrow=c(3,1)) plot(simmod2) prediction2<-predict_apc(simmod2, periods=5, population=array(1e6,c(30,10)), quantiles=c(.1,.5,.9)) plot(prediction2$cases_period[2,], ylim=range(prediction2$cases_period),ylab="",pch=19) points(prediction2$cases_period[1,],pch="–",cex=2) points(prediction2$cases_period[3,],pch="–",cex=2) for (i in 1:30)lines(rep(i,3),prediction2$cases_period[,i])

title: Bayesian Age-Period-Cohort Modeling and Prediction
text: BAMP software package analyze incidence mortality data Lexis diagram, using Bayesian version age-period-cohort model. models described , e.g., Berzuini Clayton (1994), Besag, J.E., P.J. Green, D.M. Higdon K.L. Mengersen (1995) Knorr-Held Rainer (2001). pixel Lexis diagram (specific age group specific period) data must available number persons risk (population number) number disease cases (typically cancer incidence mortality). hierarchical model assumed binomial model first-stage. smoothing priors age, period cohort parameters random walks first second order (RW1 RW2) available. BAMP also allows drop one latent components, example drop cohort effect analyze age-period model. Additional unstructured prior distributions assumed pixel Lexis diagram. Note nonidentifiability likelihood APC-model, see Clayton Schifflers (1987), indices problems interpreting latent effects. RW1 model, parameters (weakly) identifiable. BAMP several features described detailed Knorr-Held Rainer (2001): data need grid, example period can one year intervals age group five year intervals. BAMP allows prediction future number cases BAMP allows retrospective prediction model checking Additionally model described Knorr-Held Rainer (2001), BAMP can handle - AP AC models - models without global heterogenity parameter (overdispersion) - models additional age, period /cohort heterogenity - including covariates (still development) Detail feature can found Schmid (2004 - German) graphical routines available order plot estimated age, period cohort effects (RW1 model) compare observed fitted rates predict rates assess “significance” unstructured parameters. helps identify variation data, supported age, period cohort parameters.

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ data(apc) model <- bamp(cases, population, age="rw1", period="rw1", cohort="rw1", periods_per_agegroup = 5) } # }  ## Demonstration of prior_scale (no MCMC, runs instantly): for a fixed ## precision kappa, report the geometric-mean prior marginal standard ## deviation of a random-walk effect on the logit scale, with and without ## Sorbye-Rue scaling, across random-walk orders and grid sizes. prior_sd <- function(L, order, kappa = 1, scale = FALSE) {   K <- crossprod(diff(diag(L), differences = order))   # structure matrix D'D   if (scale) {                                          # Sorbye-Rue unit-variance scaling     e <- eigen(K, symmetric = TRUE); keep <- e$values > max(e$values) * 1e-9     V <- e$vectors[, keep, drop = FALSE]     Sigma <- V %*% diag(1 / e$values[keep], sum(keep)) %*% t(V)     K <- K * exp(mean(log(diag(Sigma))))   }   e <- eigen(K, symmetric = TRUE); keep <- e$values > max(e$values) * 1e-9   V <- e$vectors[, keep, drop = FALSE]   Sig <- V %*% diag(1 / e$values[keep], sum(keep)) %*% t(V) / kappa   sqrt(exp(mean(log(diag(Sig)))))                       # geometric-mean marginal SD } grid <- expand.grid(order = 1:2, L = c(10, 25, 50)) data.frame(grid,            unscaled = round(mapply(prior_sd, grid$L, grid$order, scale = FALSE), 3),            scaled   = round(mapply(prior_sd, grid$L, grid$order, scale = TRUE), 3)) #>   order  L unscaled scaled #> 1     1 10    1.224      1 #> 2     2 10    1.349      1 #> 3     1 25    1.943      1 #> 4     2 25    5.195      1 #> 5     1 50    2.749      1 #> 6     2 50   14.646      1 ## With prior_scale = FALSE the same kappa = 1 implies an effect SD ranging ## from ~1.2 to ~14.6 across these models; with prior_scale = TRUE it is 1.0 ## throughout, so a single hyper-prior on kappa means the same smoothness for ## every random-walk order and grid size.

title: bamp 3.0.0
text: Major release. Polya-Gamma sampler native C engine, identifiability-aware convergence diagnostics release contributed Chris Kypridemos. New Polya-Gamma Gibbs sampler (method = "pg", now default): joint Polya-Gamma data-augmentation sampler exact full conditionals Metropolis tuning. Supports overdispersion, age/period/cohort heterogeneity period/cohort covariates natively. legacy Taylor sampler remains available via method = "taylor". Native C implementation Polya-Gamma sampler (pg_engine = "C", default) equivalent pure-R reference (pg_engine = "R"); two agree numerical tolerance. mcmc.options values number_of_iterations, burn_in step may now set "auto" (default), chooses MCMC length rarity data. value given number used exactly . New prior_scale argument method = "pg". checkConvergence() now assesses identified quantities (smoothing precisions, intercept fitted linear predictor per Lexis cell), invariant age-period-cohort trend aliasing, rather raw effect chains drift along non-identified trend. effects.apc() plot.apc() gain convention argument fixes non-identified linear trend chosen display gauge, making effect curves reproducible runs; plot.apc() also handles number quantiles zero-covariate models. Fixed predict_apc(periods = 0) crash (downward-sequence --one). Fixed predict_apc() logit overflow: use plogis() instead exp(x)/(1+exp(x)), returned NaN large forecast logits crashed downstream. Fixed bamp(): age/period/cohort = NULL now accepted (previously errored “argument length zero”). Fixed predict_apc(): age-period models without cohort effect can now predicted, non-integer population/exposure longer produces NA. bamp(..., method = "pg"): chain fails forked parallelism (parallel::mclapply) now reports actual error instead opaque “subscript bounds” resulted silently indexing failed chain’s result.

title: bamp 2.2.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-06-21 Effects (age, period, cohort) now computed automatically inside bamp() stored returned object (model$effects), separate call effects.apc() longer needed default median summary. Fixed bug effects.apc(): cache check looking x$effect (singular) instead x$effects (plural), referenced undefined variable cache condition. MCMC chains now use warm starts: restart previous sample values used initial values, reducing burn-time automatic convergence checking. First-run behaviour unchanged. Fixed bug cohort heterogeneity hyperparameter check (cohort="rw2+het" recognized correctly). Fixed typo period_covariate handling silently prevented vector coercion. Fixed checkConvergence(): cohort convergence check used age hyperparameter instead cohort hyperparameter. Fixed hyperparameter display checkConvergence() info output. Fixed memory leaks C++ MCMC code (raw pointer allocations per iteration). Fixed GetRNGstate/PutRNGstate pairing random number generation. Added Cholesky decomposition error check informative message. Replaced fork-based mclapply socket-based makeCluster/parLapply reliable parallel execution platforms, including macOS GUI environments (RStudio). Falls back sequential cluster setup fails. MCMC chains fail due numerical errors now discarded cleanly instead continuing corrupted values. Cholesky decomposition now recovers non-positive-definite precision matrices (common RW2 priors tuning) adding increasing diagonal regularization retrying, instead aborting chain. Added unit tests. Updated CITATION use bibentry().
